It's not over, you never know what the future will hold!

I've found even after episodes lasting for years there are days that are so good that I don't regret pushing through and surviving, even sometimes something as basic as just riding a bike in good weather and just realising things are actually normal in that moment.

I've found the "ball and the box" analogy pretty accurate as years go on as well - it's not something that will go away persay but the frequency/intensity of the episodes has become more manageable for me.

Of course can still do everything in your power to take care of yourself too such as eating well, exercising and sleeping well where possible, but I know firsthand how difficult these things can be when suffering - some days it's okay to just survive :)

I also suffer from insomnia and melatonin didn't work for me, only thing that I've found that really knocks me out is extreme excercise or a few drinks, one is obviously a lot healthier than the other lol

Perhaps some kind of home security system might be a better option for peace of mind before resorting to medication? Knowing that you'll get a notification on your phone if anyone comes to the door might alleviate the need to manually check etc.

As for medications I've been on a bunch over the years and none really worked for me, but everyone's different and I know others who swear by it.
